# select_snowflake_account (Resource)

A connection to one Snowflake account: the credentials SELECT authenticates with, the role and warehouse it runs as, and how it exports data.

## About

A Snowflake account is SELECT's connection to one Snowflake account: the credentials it authenticates with, the role and warehouse it runs as, and how it exports data. To learn more, see the [SELECT documentation](https://select.dev/docs/getting-started).

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API. The `api_key` configured on the provider must carry the `snowflake_accounts:read` and `snowflake_accounts:write` scopes; without them every operation fails with an authorization error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Key pair authentication, which is what most automated setups use: Snowflake
# rejects password authentication for service users on accounts that enforce MFA.
resource "select_snowflake_account" "production" {
  id   = "acme-us-east-1"
  name = "Acme Production"

  credentials = {
    authentication_method = "key_pair"
    username              = "SELECT_USER"
    private_key           = file("${path.module}/select_user.p8")
  }

  role      = "SELECT_ROLE"
  warehouse = "SELECT_WH"

  # Exactly one export destination is required.
  export_storage_integration_name = "SELECT_STORAGE_INTEGRATION"
}

# Workload identity federation needs no secret at all: Snowflake resolves the
# user from its own workload identity mapping.
resource "select_snowflake_account" "analytics" {
  id   = "acme-analytics"
  name = "Acme Analytics"

  credentials = {
    authentication_method = "workload_identity_federation"
  }

  role              = "SELECT_ROLE"
  warehouse         = "SELECT_WH"
  export_stage_name = "SELECT_DB.PUBLIC.SELECT_EXPORT_STAGE"
  sync_enabled      = true

  # Attribute activity from these users to Fivetran rather than to the users
  # themselves.
  fivetran_users = ["FIVETRAN_USER"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `credentials` (Attributes) How SELECT authenticates to the account. The secrets in this block are stored in a secret store and never returned by the API, so SELECT cannot detect changes made to them outside Terraform. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `id` (String) The account's Snowflake identifier, in ORGANIZATION-ACCOUNT form (e.g. acme-us-east-1). Must already be normalized: lower case, no surrounding whitespace, and `-` rather than `.` between organization and account. A PrivateLink identifier, which ends in `.privatelink`, keeps its dots. Changing this forces a new Snowflake account to be added.
- `name` (String) Display name for the account, as shown throughout SELECT.

### Optional

- `compute_cost_per_credit` (Number) Overrides the credit rate SELECT reads from Snowflake when costing compute. Required together with `storage_cost_per_tb` when the account cannot read organization-level rates.
- `customer_side_sanitization_database_schema` (String) `DATABASE.SCHEMA` hosting your own sanitized copies of Snowflake's account usage views, which SELECT reads instead of the originals. Null disables the redirection.
- `customer_side_sanitization_views` (List of String) The account usage views to redirect, such as `query_history`. Null redirects every view SELECT reads. Requires `customer_side_sanitization_database_schema`.
- `describe_object_sproc_name` (String) Fully qualified name of the stored procedure SELECT calls to describe objects it cannot read directly. Null if there is none.
- `excluded_users_filter_expression` (String) JSON-encoded filter selecting Snowflake users whose activity is excluded from SELECT's cost and usage figures.
- `export_stage_name` (String) Fully qualified name of the Snowflake stage used to export data to SELECT. Mutually exclusive with `export_storage_integration_name`.
- `export_storage_integration_name` (String) Name of the Snowflake storage integration used to export data to SELECT. Mutually exclusive with `export_stage_name`.
- `fivetran_users` (List of String) Snowflake users that Fivetran runs as, so their activity is attributed to Fivetran.
- `mode_token_id` (String) Identifier of the Mode API token SELECT uses.
- `mode_token_secret` (String, Sensitive) The Mode API token secret.
- `mode_workspace` (String) The Mode workspace to attribute queries to.
- `query_sanitization_enabled` (Boolean) Whether query text is sanitized before SELECT stores it.
- `role` (String) The Snowflake role SELECT assumes when reading this account. Null uses the user's default role.
- `storage_cost_per_tb` (Number) Overrides the rate SELECT uses when costing storage, per terabyte per month. Required together with `compute_cost_per_credit` when the account cannot read organization-level rates.
- `sync_enabled` (Boolean) Whether SELECT starts syncing data for this account.
- `warehouse` (String) The Snowflake warehouse SELECT runs its queries on. Null uses the user's default warehouse.

### Read-Only

- `account_region` (String) The Snowflake region the account is hosted in.
- `added_by_email` (String) Email address of the user who added the account.
- `connection_id` (String) Identifier of the underlying connection this account reads through.
- `create_time` (String) When the account was added to SELECT, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this account. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `has_data_share` (Boolean) Whether the account reads SELECT's data share.
- `has_manage_warehouses_grant` (Boolean) Whether SELECT's role holds `manage warehouses` on the account, which smart suspension requires. Null until first checked.
- `has_org_admin_access` (Boolean) Whether SELECT can read this account's Snowflake organization-level usage views, which is what makes organization-wide rates and spend available.
- `last_successful_sync_time` (String) When the account's last sync succeeded, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp. Behind `latest_sync_time` if the most recent attempt failed.
- `latest_hourly_spend_time` (String) The most recent hour SELECT holds spend data for, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.
- `latest_sync_time` (String) When SELECT last synced data for this account, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.
- `locator` (String) The account's Snowflake locator, as returned by `current_account()`.
- `mode_credentials_configured` (Boolean) Whether Mode BI credentials are configured for this account. The credentials themselves are never returned.
- `snowflake_account_name` (String) The account's name within its Snowflake organization.
- `snowflake_organization_name` (String) Name of the Snowflake organization the account belongs to.
- `snowflake_reader_parent_account_name` (String) For a reader account, the name of the account that created it. Null for a regular account.
- `snowsight_url` (String) Link to the account in Snowsight.
- `update_time` (String) When the account was last changed, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `authentication_method` (String) Which authentication method SELECT uses for this account.

Optional:

- `password` (String, Sensitive) That user's password. Required for `password`.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) PEM-encoded private key for that user, including the `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` and `-----END PRIVATE KEY-----` lines. Required for `key_pair`.
- `private_key_passphrase` (String, Sensitive) Passphrase protecting the private key, if it is encrypted. Only valid for `key_pair`.
- `username` (String) The Snowflake user SELECT connects as. Required for `password` and `key_pair`; omitted for `workload_identity_federation`.

## Import

`select_snowflake_account` can be imported using the Snowflake account identifier:

```bash
terraform import select_snowflake_account.example acme-us-east-1
```

The identifier is the same `ORGANIZATION-ACCOUNT` value as the `id` attribute, in lower case with a `-` between the organization and account names.

An import cannot recover `credentials`: SELECT stores them in a secret store and never returns them. Put the credentials in your configuration before importing, and the first apply after the import will re-send them.

The same first plan may also show a whitespace-only change to `excluded_users_filter_expression`, because SELECT stores it as a JSON document and re-serializes it on the way out. Applying once settles it, and later plans are clean.

## Additional Information

### Creating an account validates it against Snowflake

SELECT runs a full set of checks — connectivity, permissions, account identity — before it stores anything. A create that fails leaves no account behind, and the error names the checks that did not pass along with what to change. This means `terraform apply` needs credentials that actually work, and that a Snowflake outage will fail the apply rather than store a broken connection.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the account's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the account changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.

### Deleting an account is not reversible

Destroying this resource removes the connection and the usage data SELECT has collected through it. Re-adding the same account starts its history over.

### Rotating and removing secrets

`credentials` and `mode_token_secret` are only re-sent when their configured values change, so an apply that renames the account does not rotate the stored secret.

SELECT will not clear a Mode token secret on its own. To disconnect Mode, remove `mode_workspace`; that clears the workspace, the token ID and the secret together.

### Cost rate overrides

`compute_cost_per_credit` and `storage_cost_per_tb` must be set together. They are required for accounts that cannot read organization-level rates from Snowflake, and otherwise SELECT uses the rates on the account's contract.
